item.title: Police narrative reveals murder victim from Saline County recorded his own death on cell phone
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole

item.content:encoded:
UPDATE AUG 12, 2026
EARLIER: JUL 15, 2026

Chilling details have emerged in the capital murder case with suspects Yudith Cicard Reyes and Luis Felipe Reyes-Isabel of Saline County, Arkansas. Court records reveal that the victim, Jose Miguel Quiroz-Mata, recorded his own fatal shooting on his cell phone. Read more below.




Quiroz-Mata, age 44, was found dead inside his vehicle in Little Rock on July 14, 2026, just days after he had repeatedly contacted law enforcement to report a suspected arson, escalating threats, and the physical sabotage of his vehicle.

According to an arrest affidavit from the Little Rock Police Department, officers responded to a ShotSpotter alert and subsequent shooting call at approximately 6:09 a.m. on July 14, 2026, in the 4200 block of W. 10th St.

Upon arrival, first responders located Quiroz-Mata deceased in the driver’s seat of his white Chevrolet, suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. Processing of the crime scene yielded three .380-caliber cartridge casings, shattered glass, and a projectile strike on the driver’s side door frame.

Yudith Cicard Reyes • Arrest Date: 07/14/2026 • Agency: Little Rock Police Department • Age: 49 • White Female • DOB: 05/06/1977 • Charged with: #1 warrant: affidavit-felony warrant issued by little rock police department, ar; #2 CAPITAL MURDER • NO BOND.
Luis Reyes • Arrest Date: 07/14/2026 • Agency: Little Rock Police Department • Age:22 • White Male • DOB: 10/20/2003 • Charged with: #1 warrant: affidavit-felony warrant issued by ar. NO BOND, ICE PENDING.


The breakthrough in the investigation came when detectives discovered Quiroz-Mata’s cell phone on the driver-side floorboard of his vehicle. After obtaining the passcode from family members, detectives discovered a video recording captured by the victim immediately prior to his death.

The footage captured a black truck blocking the roadway, followed by a male identified as 22-year-old Luis Felipe Reyes-Isabel approaching the victim’s vehicle with a handgun and firing five rounds inside.

Witnesses in the neighborhood reported hearing five gunshots, seeing a black truck follow a white truck, and hearing screams. One witness told detectives they specifically observed Quiroz-Mata’s ex-wife, 49-year-old Yudith Reyes, sitting in the front passenger seat of the suspect vehicle during the shooting.

Additionally, a resident’s security camera captured footage of Quiroz-Mata’s white Chevy striking a mailbox at 6:08 a.m., with the black truck trailing slowly behind it.

Using Flock license plate readers, investigators tracked the movements of a black 2026 Dodge Ram registered to Yudith Reyes. The vehicle was recorded northbound on Chicot Road at 3:30 a.m. and southbound on Cedar Street at 3:51 a.m. City surveillance cameras also captured both Yudith Reyes and Reyes-Isabel riding in the truck together on Geyer Springs Road at 6:18 a.m., minutes after the shooting.

Later that morning, detectives spotted Yudith Reyes’s second vehicle, a Chevrolet Trailblazer, at an office strip at the 10600 of Colonel Glenn Road, and took her into custody without incident.

Investigators subsequently executed a search-and-seizure warrant at her home located in the Royal Oaks neighborhood in Mabelvale. Inside the residence, police recovered a Ruger .380-caliber gun box, a paycheck stub for Reyes-Isabel, and his state fisheries conservation license.

After being read her Miranda rights, Yudith Reyes provided a recorded statement admitting that Reyes-Isabel drove the truck to the crime scene, shot Quiroz-Mata, and fled.

Although she initially claimed Reyes-Isabel was her cousin, family members refuted that assertion to police. Both suspects are currently being held without bond at the Pulaski County Regional Jail on charges of capital murder. Mr. Reyes-Isabel has a case pending with Immigration & Customs Enforcement (ICE).

The arrest affidavit also reveals that Mr. Quiroz-Mata had spent weeks pleading with authorities for assistance as the situation escalated. On June 15, 2026, he reported to police that his ex-wife may have been responsible for a house fire.

On July 9, he filed a formal harassment complaint at the prosecuting attorney’s office. Finally, on July 12 — just 48 hours before he was killed — Quiroz-Mata filed a police report stating that Reyes’s boyfriend had physically sabotaged his vehicle.

item.title: Convicted Saline County double-murderer Timothy Wallace seeks executive clemency from Arkansas governor
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: Timothy Wallace, a Saline County man convicted in 2007 of the double murder of his ex-wife and her acquaintance, is seeking executive clemency from the Governor of Arkansas. State authorities are currently accepting public feedback on the application ahead of a scheduled review by the Arkansas Parole Board. Read more below. The application for Executive […]
item.content:encoded:
Timothy Wallace, a Saline County man convicted in 2007 of the double murder of his ex-wife and her acquaintance, is seeking executive clemency from the Governor of Arkansas. State authorities are currently accepting public feedback on the application ahead of a scheduled review by the Arkansas Parole Board. Read more below.




The application for Executive Clemency Commutation filed by Wallace, Timothy ADC#139107, was formally published in a legal notice in accordance with Arkansas state law. His petition will undergo a formal review by the Arkansas Parole Board during the month of October 2026.

Members of the public who wish to comment or express their opinions on Wallace’s application for executive clemency may write to Institutional Release Services, 2801 South Olive Street, Suite 6D, Pine Bluff, Arkansas 71603. To be considered in the review process, all written correspondence must be received prior to August 22, 2026.

The case dates back to the early morning hours of June 26, 2005, when Wallace was age 38. According to court records, Wallace placed a call himself to 911 at approximately 2:30 a.m. indicating that he had shot his former wife, Brandy Wallace, and her male acquaintance, Billy Hassel, at the home the couple had previously shared.

Wallace had surrendered the home to Brandy in an uncontested divorce decree filed just nine days prior to the incident. During the 911 call, which lasted for several hours, Wallace repeatedly threatened suicide and refused to disclose his whereabouts. Saline County sheriff’s deputies eventually located and apprehended him inside his parked pickup truck in a rural section of the county.

At trial, Wallace claimed that he had returned to the home to retrieve personal belongings and shot Hassel in self-defense, asserting that Brandy’s death was accidental. However, forensic evidence presented by the state medical examiner showed that Brandy was shot multiple times at close range while holding her car keys and her cellular phone, while Hassel suffered three gunshot wounds—including shots originating from behind—and severe blunt force trauma consistent with being struck by the butt of a gun.

On June 14, 2007, a Saline County Circuit Court jury convicted Wallace of two counts of capital murder. He was subsequently sentenced on June 18, 2007, to two consecutive terms of life imprisonment without the possibility of parole. At this point, 21 years have passed.

Wallace filed several subsequent appeals, arguing various points of trial error, ineffective assistance of counsel, and actual innocence, all of which were subsequently denied or dismissed by the Arkansas Supreme Court and the federal district court.

Having exhausted all standard legal appeals, executive clemency represents his final remaining option for sentence commutation.

FULL LEGAL NOTICE IS AS FOLLOWS:

The notice of application for Executive Clemency of Wallace, Timothy ADC#139107 is hereby published as required by Arkansas Code Ann. §5-4-607. Wallace, Timothy ADC#139107 was convicted in Saline County, Arkansas on June 14, 2007 of Capital Murder. His information will be reviewed before the Arkansas Parole Board during the month of October , 2026. Wallace, Timothy ADC#139107 is requesting that the Governor of Arkansas grant him Executive Clemency Commutation. Individuals wishing to comment or express their opinions on this application for Executive Clemency may write to Institutional Release Services, 2801 South Olive Street, Suite 6D, Pine Bluff, Arkansas 71603, prior to August 22, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
UPDATE: AUG 5, 2026 4:30PM
ORIGINAL: AUG 4, 2026, 11AM

Newly released police and court documents reveal that a Shannon Hills police officer arrested Tuesday on domestic assault charges has a history of prior domestic incidents involving the same victim dating back to 2021. Joaquin Silvestre Alvarado, 37, was placed on administrative leave after his arrest early Tuesday morning, which has now brought past allegations to light. Read more below.




According to an arrest report from the Little Rock Police Department, Alvarado was taken into custody near his home at approximately 2:30 a.m. on August 4, 2026. Officers responded to a disturbance call where Alvarado was accused of assaulting two victims using a flashlight. Before officers arrived, Alvarado allegedly threw the flashlight into a nearby wooded area in an attempt to discard the evidence.

Alvarado is facing two counts of third-degree assault on a family or household member, one count of tampering with physical evidence for destroying or throwing away the flashlight, and one count of first-degree criminal mischief for property damage totaling $1,000 or less.

Alvarado underwent a video arraignment in criminal court on Tuesday morning. Then in an afternoon court appearance, a judge set his bail at $1,000 and issued a strict no-contact order. Under the court order, Alvarado is barred from having any direct or indirect contact with the victim or the victim’s immediate family, including via phone, computer, mail, or in person. His trial has been scheduled for September 2, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. in Little Rock District Court.

According to court records, Alvarado bonded out at around 10:00 a.m. August 5, 2026, with the help of Bobby Cox Bail Bonds.

The Shannon Hills Police Department, where Alvarado has served as an officer for approximately four years, confirmed they have taken custody of his service weapon, badge, and departmental identification, placing him on immediate administrative leave.

As part of the active investigation, Little Rock police detectives reviewed and included records of past domestic abuse complaints filed against Alvarado. The files show a pattern of behavior involving the same victim over several years:

On December 13, 2021, Little Rock police officers responded to a domestic disturbance. The responding officer, Officer Pool, reported that the victim accused Alvarado of grabbing her left wrist and pushing her to the ground, causing pain. The physical altercation was witnessed by two juveniles. While a no-contact order was initially put in place during the legal proceedings, court records show the victim appeared in court in May 2022 to request that the protection order be vacated. The case was ultimately resolved on October 27, 2023.

On December 6, 2023, police responded to another domestic situation involving the couple. Although a court-ordered Order of Protection was initially requested and issued, court records show that the petitioner—the same victim as in the current 2026 case—requested that the order be dismissed shortly thereafter.

Summary of current charges:

  • Two counts of third-degree assault on a family or household member
  • One count of tampering with physical evidence (destroying evidence)
  • One count of first-degree criminal mischief (damages for collecting insurance of $1,000 or less)

Representatives for the justice system note that all charges and allegations contained in arrest reports and court filings are accusations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in a court of law.
